newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Zaire opposition says against foreign intervention.
newsitem.headline: Zaire opposition says against foreign intervention.

text.p: Two leading Zairean opposition parties said on Friday they opposed foreign military intervention in the east of the country to allow distribution of aid to hundreds of thousands of refugees.

Spokespeople for the Union for Democracy and Social Progress (UDPS) and Democratic Christian Social Party (PDSC) told a news conference in Brussels that aid should be distributed in neighbouring Rwanda and Burundi only, not in Zaire.
"We want the Rwandan refugees back in their country, therefore humanitarian aid must be distributed there and not in Zaire," UDPS spokeswoman Justine M'Poyo Kasa-Vubu said.
"We do not want the refugees to settle there," she added.
The refugees -- mainly ethnic Hutus who fled the two countries after bloody ethnic conflict there -- would be forced to return to their homelands if the aid was there, she said.
More than one million refugees have been cut off from aid by a multi-sided war in eastern Zaire which has scattered them from their camps.

PDSC spokesman Albert M'Peti said there could be no question of a foreign military force entering Zaire. France and Spain have led European efforts to set up a military intervention force which would help bring aid to the refugees and safeguard their return home via so-called "humanitarian corridors".
"(Zairean Prime Minister) Kengo and (President) Mobutu want to allow a foreign force in Zaire before the repatriation of the refugees. There can be no question of that," Kasa-Vubu said.
Kasa-Vubu -- daughter of Zaire's first president Joseph Kasa-Vubu -- said French troops were not wanted on Zairean soil.

"We are hostile to a French presence in eastern Zaire. France is not a neutral power. (President) Chirac has sided with the Kengo/Mobutu camp and with the authors of the (1994) genocide in Rwanda," she said.
Both spokespeople said they did not want a "Hutu land" created within Zaire.
"The governments of Rwanda and Burundi refuse to let their Hutu population return. They want to create a Hutu-land in Zaire," PDSC's M'Peti said.
"The creation of a Hutu-land is tantamount to a redefinition of the eastern Zairean borders, which is unacceptable," Kasa-Vubu said.
M'Peti also called on the Zaire government to stop servicing its debts to the World Bank, which he said cost Zaire $5 million every month.
"Kengo prefers paying the debt rather than paying Zairean soldiers and government officials. I think the payments to the World Bank can wait until the economy recovers," he said.
Both spokespeople called for the resignation of the Kengo government and called for a government of national unity.
